newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Vietnamese migrants say U.S. reneged on promise.
newsitem.headline: Vietnamese migrants say U.S. reneged on promise.

text.p: Scores of Vietnamese Amerasians protested outside the United States Embassy in the Philippine capital of Manila on Wednesday and accused Washington of breaking its promise to resettle them in America.
The estimated 80 protestors are among about 1,000 Vietnamese migrants stranded in a camp on southwestern Palawan island after being denied asylum in the United States and other Western countries.
They carried signs reading "America keep your promise" and "No food, no education, no country, no freedom. U.S., this not what you promised."

The protesters said they belonged to a group of Amerasians, children of American servicemen who served in Vietnam, who came to the Philippines several years ago to be trained in American culture prior to being resettled in the United States under a repatriation programme agreed on by Hanoi and Washington.
They were stuck in the Philippines after U.S. officials accused them of carrying fraudulent papers or having "anti-social tendencies," said the group's spokeswoman, Nguyen Thi Kim Nguyen.

"We were interviewed in Vietnam and determined by American consular officers as fully eligible to resettle in the United States," she told reporters. "But when we came here they found fault with our cases."
Filipino Roman Catholic bishop Ramon Arguelles, who accompanied the group, said the problem of the Vietnamese Amerasians was a concern of the United States and Vietnam.
"The Philippines is a kind of dumping ground, which is unfair," he said.
A U.S. Embassy official said the matter was being studied in Washington. "We are looking for a humane and just resolution of this rather complex situation," said the official.
Most of the 1,000 Vietnamese still in Palawan were denied asylum after United Nations officials determined that most of them were economic migrants and not refugees fleeing political persecution.
A church group is taking care of them in the camp.
